_doc: Every number the engine uses, with where it comes from. 'source' = checked against a page; 'estimate' = our judgement, open to revision.

meters_per_unit.why: terrain is projected from real coordinates: OSM coastline + SRTM 30 m elevation, origin lon 28.884 / lat 41.058, map 14.4 x 9.6 km

wall_gap_m.note: Constantine's wall ~2.8 km (15 stadia) west of the Severan wall; Theodosian walls ~2 km further west

population_330.note: one study gives ~30,000 in 330 and ~300,000 by 450

population_450.note: Growing Up in Constantinople (2015) via search; mid-5th c. urban area ~1,400 ha

grain_dole_332.note: 80,000 rations a day from 117 distribution points

people_per_house.why: house footprint 10-16 m, 2-3 storeys; at ~50% built cover gives ~260 people/ha, inside the 100-400/ha range of dense pre-industrial cities

growth_cap_per_decade.why: historic average 330-450 is ~21%/decade (x10 in 120 years); booms run faster, so the cap sits above the average

food.why: two harbors + one granary ~ 80,000, the size of the 332 grain dole

water.why: wells and rain for a small town; a full aqueduct system supports a metropolis of hundreds of thousands

terrain.coastline: OpenStreetMap natural=coastline via Overpass, 2026-10-09 (modern shoreline, includes landfill)
terrain.landmarks: placed at real lat/lon: Milion, Hagia Sophia/Irene, Hippodrome, Forum of Constantine, Binbirdirek, Kumkapi, Sirkeci, Severan & Constantinian wall lines (approx.)

aqueduct_arcade_rule.why: Gravity channel falls evenly from source to end; where the ground lies more than 6 m below the channel it must ride on arcades. Applies to aqueducts built from AF 11 on; the small old channel of era 0 is treated as a ground-level/underground conduit and grandfathered.

grammar_rule.why: Architectural grammar v0.2 §11 (docs/arch-grammar-draft.md). Buildings proposed from AF 21 on must declare dna.motif allowed for their type; earlier eras are grandfathered so published history does not change. Exempt types (roads, walls, aqueducts, harbors, districts, arcades, ruin markers) need no motif.

wonder_max_area.unit: sq units (1 unit = 12 m, so ~17,000 m2)
wonder_max_area.why: Hagia Sophia with its atrium covers roughly 10,000 m2 (~70 sq units); 120 leaves room for a larger rival but stops a 'wonder' the size of a district. Fit after the first century.

wonder_concurrency.why: At most one wonder-scale building may be begun per decade (§11.4, owner-approved 2026-10-10): stops wonder inflation.

memorial_wonder_threshold.why: Demolishing a structure with wonder_score >= 3 must declare memorial {kind: stele|rename|chronicle_feature, note} (§7).

independent_dice.why: disasters must not depend on what was proposed; from AF 21 fire, earthquake and plague draw from a stream seeded only by the era. Earlier eras keep the old shared stream so published history does not change.

farmland.why: Ancient Mediterranean wheat yields ran about 400-620 kg/ha (Greece 620 kg/ha in the 1920s; Roman-army logistics models use ~385-514 kg/ha), a person ate about 200-250 kg of grain a year, and biennial fallow halves the sown area: roughly 1-1.5 people per hectare of farmland. This is why the city lived on sea-borne grain (the annona from Egypt) and its fields only added a margin.
farmland.slope_why: ploughland needs gentle ground: 80% of a field must slope under 10% (our judgement; terraces would allow more, not modelled)
